title: Ordinary minimal pairs of Turing degrees
summary: Construct two noncomputable sets whose common Turing lower bounds are all computable, by deciding whether two finite oracle computations can disagree.
abstract: Incomparability compares two membership problems, while a common lower bound measures information recoverable from both. We construct two noncomputable sets for which every membership problem decidable using either set is already computable without an oracle. At each stage, two proposed oracle programs either have compatible finite computations with unequal outputs, or every common total output can be recovered by a fixed ordinary search. Separate diagonal steps keep both sets noncomputable. Their degrees consequently have greatest lower bound zero. The construction makes no claim that its sets are computably enumerable.
